title: Bytown Is Settled
description: Upper and Lower Bytown becomes available for residency.

title: The Shiners' War Begins
description: The construction of the Rideau Canal is complete, leaving the Irish navvies out of work. They banded together to find with work with the help from Peter Aylen. The group called themselves the Shiners.

title: The Perley Home
description: William Goodhue Perley builds his house along Wellington Street. The house later becomes the Perley Home.

title: Upper Town Expropriation
description: The Federal Government expropriates the properties north of Wellington Street for future projects.

title: CBC Offices Open
description: The Canadian Radio Broadcasting Commission, precursor to the CBC, sets up offices at 41 Cliff Street.

title: Last House Demolished in Upper Town
description: The last building in Upper Town, 41 Cliff Street, is demolished.

title: Hull Explosion of 1910
description: A devastating explosion occurs at the General Explosives of Montreal Ltd. factory in Hul, Quebec. 11 people die and many are injured from flying stones.

title: Standish Hall Hotel
description: The Standish Hall Hotel opens to guests and patrons.

title: Fire Destroys Standish Hall
description: The Standish Hall Hotel suffers from a devastating fire which destroys the original part of the hotel.

title: First Public Viewing of Film
description: The Holland Brothers have the first public viewing of a film using the vitascope in West End Park.

title: Smallpox Outbreak
description: A smallpox outbreak occurs in Ottawa. As a result, an isolation hospital is setup on Porter Island.

title: Hopewell Hospital Opens
description: After years of reported horrid conditions on Porter Island, the state-of-the-art Hopewell Hospital opens to take in smallpox patients.

title: Russell House Hotel Opens
description: James Gouin purchases the Campbell House Hotel at the corner of Elgin and Sparks, renovates it and renames it the Russell House Hotel. After further renovations in 1880, the hotel became an impressive sight in the young capital.

title: Fire at the Russell House Hotel!
description: 3 years after it had closed, the Russell House Hotel is destroyed in a spectacular fire watched by thousands of spectators.

title: Ottawa City Passenger Railway Founded
description: The Legislative Council Assembly of Canada granted a perpetual charter to the Ottawa City Passenger Railway. By 1870, horse drawn streetcars were in service in Ottawa.

title: The Great Epizootic
description: The Great Epizootic, a global-wide equine influenza, causes interuptions and cancelled trips for Ottawa streetcars.

title: Ottawa Electric Street Railway Incorporated
description: The Ottawa Electric Street Railway is incorporated by Thomas Ahearn and Warren Soper.

title: Two Streetcar Companies Merge
description: The Ottawa City Passenger Railway and the Ottawa Electric Street Railway merge to form the Ottawa Electric Railway Company (OER).

title: Britannia-on-the-Bay Opens
description: The OER's amusement park and beach, Britannia-on-the-Bay, opens along with Britannia streetcar line 3 days earlier.

title: OER Workers Strike!
description: OER workers go on strike. The strike lasts until July 26.
